# Capacity Planning and Sizing {#capacity-planning-and-sizing}

This guide gives you the formulas, worked numbers and measurement steps to size a host and its network before you deploy. One instance is one coherent receiver chain: `rtl_daq.out → rebuffer.out → decimate.out → delay_sync.py → [iq_server.out | shmem]`, plus `hw_controller.py`. Every number below is per instance unless a row says otherwise.

Status of the tooling:

| Tool | State |
|---|---|
| `Firmware/daq_preflight.py`, `Firmware/_daq_core/capacity_model.py` | Present. Section 8 shows their real output. |
| `heimdall-ctl capacity` | Present. It runs `daq_preflight.py` and maps its exit code. |
| `Firmware/_daq_core/frame_sizes.h` | Present. It holds the C segment-size helpers that the formulas below mirror. |
| `Firmware/_testing/iq_latency_probe.py` | Planned (WP-20), not in this release. Section 9.2 describes the design. |
| `Firmware/_testing/unit_test/test_throughput_lane.py` and its `throughput.json` | Planned (WP-17b), not in this release. Section 9.3 describes the design. |
| Measured throughput | `TBD`. No `throughput.json` exists yet (see [Measured results](#94-measured-results)). |

Related documents: [scaling_and_clustering.md](scaling_and_clustering.html), [deployment_recipes.md](deployment_recipes.html), [hardware_setup.md](hardware_setup.html), [networking_and_time_sync.md](networking_and_time_sync.html), [operations_runbook.md](operations_runbook.html), [configuration.md](configuration.html), [architecture.md](architecture.html), [consumer_guide.md](consumer_guide.html).

## 1. Key numbers at the defaults

One instance with the shipped values (5 channels, 2.4 MS/s, `cpi_size = 2^20`, `decimation_ratio = 1`, shmem output) needs the following.

| Resource | Need | What limits it |
|---|---|---|
| CPU cores | 4, pinned, real-time | `nproc` |
| USB ingress | 24.0 MB/s on one USB 2.0 bus | about 35 MB/s usable per high-speed bus (planning budget) |
| RAM (pre-flight need) | 325 MiB per instance, plus 512 MiB headroom per host = 837 MiB for one instance | `MemAvailable` in `/proc/meminfo` |
| `/dev/shm` resident | 180 MiB | `/dev/shm` free space and RAM |
| `/dev/shm` object size | 740 MiB (180 MiB with `size_segments_from_config = 1`) | `/dev/shm` size |
| `rtl_daq` ring (locked, pre-faulted) | 20 MiB | RAM (`rtl_daq` runs as root under `mlockall`) |
| usbfs transfer buffers | 30 MiB | `usbfs_memory_mb` (the start script sets it to 0 = unlimited) |
| Frame period | 0.437 s (2.29 frames/s) | control timeouts above 5 s, see section 7 |
| `:5000` egress per client | 96 MB/s = 768 Mbit/s | only with `[data_interface] out_data_iface_type = eth` (shipped: `shmem`, no `:5000` egress); one GbE link carries one such client |

The RAM row is the figure `daq_preflight.py` uses (section 8.1). The 325 MiB per instance is the locked rings (`rtl_daq` ring 20 MiB, usbfs transfers 30 MiB, rebuffer ring 15 MiB), the resident shared memory (180 MiB) and the `delay_sync.py` per-frame copies (80 MiB). It excludes the `decimate.out` FIR work buffers (16 MiB) and the memory of the Python processes (numpy, numba). The 512 MiB headroom covers those and the OS. Compare it with `grep MemAvailable /proc/meminfo`.

The shipped config writes its output to shared memory, so no `iq_server.out` runs. To serve IQ frames on `:5000`, set this in `daq_chain_config.ini`:

```ini
[data_interface]
out_data_iface_type = eth
```

The short rules that follow from this:

* Give each hardware instance its own 4 cores. A 4-core Raspberry Pi 4 or Pi 5 runs one hardware instance.
* Give each KrakenSDR its own USB 2.0 bus. Two units on one high-speed bus exceed the planning budget.
* A remote consumer of an undecimated 5-channel stream needs a full GbE link. Raise `decimation_ratio` to cut it. First set `[pre_processing] fir_tap_size` above the ratio (for example 64): the shipped value is 1, and `ini_checker.py` exits 1 otherwise. Decimation also lowers the sample rate and bandwidth that the downstream DSP sees.

## 2. Resource model per instance

### 2.1 Symbols and defaults

| Symbol | Key | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `M` | `[hw] num_ch` | 5 |
| `fs` | `[daq] sample_rate` | 2 400 000 |
| `B` | `[daq] daq_buffer_size` | 262144 (2^18) |
| `Ncpi` | `[pre_processing] cpi_size` | 1048576 (2^20) |
| `R` | `[pre_processing] decimation_ratio` | 1 |
| `Nc` | `[calibration] corr_size` | 65536 (2^16) |
| `ring` | `[daq] usb_ring_buffers` | 8 (2..64) |
| `xfer` | `[daq] usb_async_transfers` | 12 (2..64) |

### 2.2 Formulas

Each shared-memory hop has two segments (`_A` and `_B`). The formulas below include that factor of 2.

| Quantity | Formula | Default | Source in code |
|---|---|---|---|
| USB ingress | `M*fs*2` B/s | 24.0 MB/s | `rtl_daq.c` (u8 I/Q, 2 bytes per sample) |
| usbfs / libusb transfers | `M*xfer*2B` | 30 MiB | `rtl_daq.c` `rtlsdr_read_async(..., async_buf_number, buffer_size)` |
| `rtl_daq` ring (locked, pre-faulted) | `M*ring*2B` | 20 MiB | `rtl_daq.c` `malloc(num_buff * buffer_size)` after `mlockall(MCL_CURRENT \| MCL_FUTURE)` |
| `rebuffer` ring (private, locked on touch) | `M*max(Ncpi*R/B+2, Nc/B+2)*2B` (integer division) | 15 MiB | `rebuffer.c` `buffer_num_data`, `buffer_num_cal` |
| `decimator_in` object (u8) | `2*(1024 + max(Ncpi*R, Nc)*M*2)` | 20 MiB | `hd_decimator_in_object_bytes()` |
| `decimator_in` consumer map (virtual only) | `2*(1024 + max(Ncpi*R, Nc)*M*8)` | 80 MiB | `hd_decimator_in_consumer_map_bytes()` |
| `decimator_out` resident | `2*(1024 + max(Ncpi, Nc)*M*8)` | 80 MiB | `hd_iq_frame_bytes()` |
| `decimator_out` object, default | `2*(1024 + 2^23*M*8)` | 640 MiB | `hd_worst_frame_bytes()` |
| `decimator_out` object, `size_segments_from_config = 1` | `2*(1024 + max(Ncpi, Nc)*M*8)` | 80 MiB | `fir_decimate.c` |
| `delay_sync_iq` | `2*(1024 + max(Ncpi, Nc)*M*8)` | 80 MiB | `delay_sync.py` `out_shmem_size` |
| `delay_sync_hwc` | `2*1024` | 2 KiB | header only |
| `delay_sync` per-frame copy | read `Ncpi*M*8` + write `Ncpi*M*8` | 40 + 40 MiB per frame | `delay_sync.py` |
| `decimate.out` FIR work buffers | `Ncpi*R*8 + Ncpi*8` | 16 MiB | `fir_decimate.c` (allocated even at `R = 1`, where the FIR is bypassed) |
| Frame period `T_fp` | `Ncpi*R/fs` | 0.437 s | `rebuffer.c`, `ini_checker.frame_period_sec()` |
| cf32 egress per `:5000` client | `M*fs*8/R` B/s | 96 MB/s | cf32 = 8 bytes per complex sample |
| Cores pinned | 4 | 4 | `daq_start_sm.sh` |

Three sizes describe a shared-memory object. Keep them apart when you compare with limits:

* **Object size** is what `ftruncate` sets. It is the conservative figure for the `/dev/shm` size limit.
* **Resident size** is what the chain actually writes. Pages past the written frame stay untouched and cost no RAM.
* **Consumer map** is what `decimate.out` maps of `decimator_in`. It is 4 times the object because it maps 8 bytes per complex sample. Pages past the object end are never touched. It is a virtual size only and is never compared with a limit.

At the defaults the `/dev/shm` resident total is `20 + 80 + 80 = 180 MiB`. The object total is `20 + 640 + 80 = 740 MiB`. `[pre_processing] size_segments_from_config = 1` sizes `decimator_out` from the config and makes `iq_server.out` map exactly what `delay_sync.py` created, so the object total drops to 180 MiB.

**Locked memory is more than the `rtl_daq` ring.** `rtl_daq.out` calls `mlockall(MCL_CURRENT | MCL_FUTURE)` before it allocates its ring, so the ring and every later mapping are locked and pre-faulted. `rebuffer.out`, `decimate.out` and `iq_server.out` call `mlockall(MCL_CURRENT | MCL_FUTURE | MCL_ONFAULT)`. They lock every page they touch, not the untouched rest of a mapping. The pinned RAM is therefore roughly the rings, the FIR work buffers and the resident shared-memory pages each process touches. `daq_preflight.py` models the largest per-process locked set as follows (defaults):

| Process | Locked set | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `rtl_daq.out` | `rtl_daq` ring + usbfs transfers | 50 MiB |
| `rebuffer.out` | rebuffer ring + `decimator_in` | 35 MiB |
| `decimate.out` | `decimator_in` + `decimator_out` resident | 100 MiB |
| `iq_server.out` (eth output only) | `delay_sync_iq` | 80 MiB |

The `memlock` check compares the largest of these (100 MiB) with `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK`. The model leaves out the FIR work buffers.

### 2.3 Flow control per hop

A slow consumer downstream of `decimate.out` drops frames at the first drop-mode hop upstream of it. It never stalls USB ingress. A slow `decimate.out` back-pressures `rebuffer.out` and the USB ring.

| Hop | Mode (shipped start scripts) |
|---|---|
| `rtl_daq.out` → `rebuffer.out` | stdout pipe, blocking |
| `rebuffer.out` → `decimate.out` (`decimator_in`) | back-pressure (`rebuffer.out 0`) |
| `decimate.out` → `delay_sync.py` (`decimator_out`) | drop (`decimate.out` with no argument) |
| `delay_sync.py` → `iq_server.out` (`delay_sync_iq`) | drop |
| `delay_sync.py` → `hw_controller.py` (`delay_sync_hwc`) | drop |

`decimate.out` itself sits on the back-pressure side. If FIR decimation cannot keep up, `rebuffer.out` blocks, the stdout pipe fills and `rtl_daq.out` logs `USB ring-buffer overrun` while header slot 102 rises. Reduce `fir_tap_size` or change `[offload] fir_engine` before you deepen the USB ring (section 6.1).

### 2.4 Cores and real-time priorities

`daq_start_sm.sh` pins instance `N` to cores `CORE_k = (N*4 + k) % nproc` for `k = 0..3` when `[host] cpu_cores` is empty. For instance `N > 0` with `nproc < (N+1)*4` it only prints a `WARN:` line and the instances share cores. `[host] cpu_cores` replaces this layout (section 11).

| SCHED_FIFO priority | Process | Core |
|---|---|---|
| 99 | `rtl_daq.out` | `CORE0` |
| 94 | `rebuffer.out` | `CORE1` |
| 92 | `decimate.out` | `CORE1` |
| 90 | `delay_sync.py` | `CORE2` |
| 88 | `iq_server.out` (eth output only) | `CORE2` |
| 82 | `hw_controller.py` | `CORE3` |

`[host] rt_priority_offset` subtracts the same amount from every priority. `iq_server.out` shares core 2 with `delay_sync.py`. On hosts with fewer than 4 cores and an empty `cpu_cores` the script falls back: with 3 cores `delay_sync.py` keeps `CORE2`, with 2 it moves to `CORE1`, and `hw_controller.py` and `iq_server.out` run unpinned. `daq_synthetic_start.sh` without `--rt` pins nothing and only runs `decimate.out` under `chrt -f 99`.

## 3. Worked numbers

### 3.1 One instance, 5 channels at 2.4 MS/s, `cpi_size = 2^20`

Raising `decimation_ratio` leaves USB ingress unchanged. It cuts egress and the output sample rate, and it lengthens the frame period. It grows the rebuffer ring and `decimator_in`. Every `R > 1` column needs `[pre_processing] fir_tap_size > R` (for example 64); the shipped `fir_tap_size = 1` makes `ini_checker.py` exit 1.

| Quantity | R = 1 (default) | R = 2 | R = 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| USB ingress | 24.0 MB/s | 24.0 MB/s | 24.0 MB/s |
| Frame period `T_fp` | 0.437 s | 0.874 s | 1.748 s |
| Output sample rate | 2.4 MS/s | 1.2 MS/s | 0.6 MS/s |
| `:5000` egress per client (eth output) | 96 MB/s (768 Mbit/s) | 48 MB/s (384 Mbit/s) | 24 MB/s (192 Mbit/s) |
| `rtl_daq` ring (locked) | 20 MiB | 20 MiB | 20 MiB |
| usbfs transfers | 30 MiB | 30 MiB | 30 MiB |
| `rebuffer` ring | 15 MiB | 25 MiB | 45 MiB |
| `decimator_in` object | 20 MiB | 40 MiB | 80 MiB |
| `decimator_in` consumer map (virtual) | 80 MiB | 160 MiB | 320 MiB |
| `decimator_out` resident / object | 80 / 640 MiB | 80 / 640 MiB | 80 / 640 MiB |
| `delay_sync_iq` | 80 MiB | 80 MiB | 80 MiB |
| `/dev/shm` resident | 180 MiB | 200 MiB | 240 MiB |
| `/dev/shm` objects (default / config-sized) | 740 / 180 MiB | 760 / 200 MiB | 800 / 240 MiB |
| RAM per instance (pre-flight model, no headroom) | 325 MiB | 355 MiB | 415 MiB |
| `decimate.out` FIR work buffers | 16 MiB | 24 MiB | 40 MiB |
| FIR MAC rate, KFR (`2*taps*M*fs`) | FIR bypassed | `24e6*taps`/s | `24e6*taps`/s |
| FIR MAC rate, generic (`2*taps*M*fs/R`) | FIR bypassed | `12e6*taps`/s | `6e6*taps`/s |

`ini_checker.py` and `fir_filter_designer.py` refuse `fir_tap_size <= decimation_ratio` when `decimation_ratio != 1`. Pick the tap count first, then read the MAC rate from the last two rows.

### 3.2 Several instances on one host (defaults, eth output, one client each)

| Host total | 1 instance | 2 instances | 4 instances |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pinned cores | 4 | 8 | 16 |
| USB ingress | 24 MB/s | 48 MB/s (2 buses) | 96 MB/s (4 buses) |
| RAM (pre-flight need, incl. 512 MiB headroom) | 837 MiB | 1162 MiB | 1812 MiB |
| `/dev/shm` resident | 180 MiB | 360 MiB | 720 MiB |
| `/dev/shm` objects, default | 740 MiB | 1480 MiB | 2960 MiB |
| `/dev/shm` objects, `size_segments_from_config = 1` | 180 MiB | 360 MiB | 720 MiB |
| `rtl_daq` rings only (locked) | 20 MiB | 40 MiB | 80 MiB |
| `:5000` egress, remote consumers | 96 MB/s | 192 MB/s | 384 MB/s |

The egress row applies only when each consumer sits on another host. With shmem output, or a consumer on the same host, nothing leaves the NIC. Two remote undecimated streams do not fit one GbE link.

Prerequisites for more than one hardware instance per host:

* Program unit `k` to EEPROM serials `1000 + 100*k + i` for channel `i`. Factory units all carry 1000..1004, and a second instance cannot open them.
* In the INI of instance `k`, set `[federation] instance_id = k` and `[hw] serial_base = 1000 + 100*k` (or `[hw] device_serials`). Set `[daq] ctr_channel_serial_no` to one of those serials, normally `serial_base`.
* Attach each unit to its own USB bus (section 4.3).
* Run each instance from its own instance directory.

See [configuration.md](configuration.html) for the serial keys and [scaling_and_clustering.md](scaling_and_clustering.html) section 4.4 and [deployment_recipes.md](deployment_recipes.html) Recipe C for the full procedure. `daq_preflight.py --add-instances N` plans extra instances with these serial and core defaults (section 8).

### 3.3 IQ router memory bound

The IQ router (`federation_iq_router.py`, `:7000`) is opt-in. Start it by hand from `Firmware/`:

```
python3 _daq_core/federation_iq_router.py --config federation.ini
```

It holds bounded per-client queues. Its worst-case memory is:

```
frame_bytes * (queue_frames * max_clients + align_max_frames * sources + sources)
```

The three queue parameters are `[federation]` keys of `federation.ini`. A CLI flag wins over the key.

| Parameter | Key in `federation.ini` | CLI flag | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frame_bytes` | derived: `1024 + max(Ncpi, Nc)*M*8` | none | 41 944 064 B (40.0 MiB) |
| `queue_frames` | `router_queue_frames` | `--queue-frames` | 4 |
| `max_clients` | `router_max_clients` | `--max-clients` | 8 |
| `align_max_frames` | `router_align_max_frames` | `--align-max-frames` | 2 |

With 2 sources at the defaults: `40 MiB * (32 + 4 + 2) = 1.48 GiB` (1 593 874 432 B). The router logs this bound in bytes at start only when its `--config` file carries `[hw] num_ch` and `[pre_processing] cpi_size`. Otherwise the start line shows `N frames x frame size (learned from the first frame)`.

Every router client receives every source. One `:7000` client of two undecimated 5-channel sources needs 192 MB/s, which is more than one GbE link. See [scaling_and_clustering.md](scaling_and_clustering.html) section 7 for the router setup.

## 4. Host budgets

### 4.1 Core-count rule

Each hardware instance needs its own 4 cores for its 4 real-time tiers. Count before you deploy:

```
4 * hardware_instances > nproc   ->  does not fit
```

The start script only warns when cores are shared. `daq_preflight.py` turns the rule into a `fail` verdict, or a `warn` when every planned instance sets `[host] allow_core_sharing = allow`.

At start time, `allow_core_sharing = refuse` or `warn` acts only with `[host] instance_registry = 1`. The core guard compares this instance's cores with those of the other live registry entries. Without the registry it does nothing beyond the plain `WARN:` line of section 2.4.

### 4.2 Host classes

| Host | Hardware instances | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Raspberry Pi 4 (4 cores) | 1 | `util/irq_tuning.sh` assumes 4 cores on aarch64. Default `size_segments_from_config = 0` creates 740 MiB of `/dev/shm` objects; on small-RAM boards set it to 1. Check RAM against the 837 MiB of section 1. |
| Raspberry Pi 5 (4 cores) | 1 | Its RP1 USB buses are independent, but the 4 cores are the limit. The pre-flight `board` check warns for more than one hardware instance. |
| 8-core x86 with two xHCI controllers | 2 | Instance 0 on cores 0-3, instance 1 on cores 4-7 (the default `(N*4+k) % nproc` layout). Attach each KrakenSDR to a different controller. Meet the prerequisites of section 3.2 first. |
| 16-core x86 with four controllers | 4 | Check `/dev/shm` objects (2960 MiB at default sizing) and egress (section 3.2). Meet the prerequisites of section 3.2 first. |

Measured per-host results stay `TBD` until the throughput lane has run on that host (section 9.3).

`tmpfs` mounts `/dev/shm` at half of RAM by default on most distributions. Check `df -h /dev/shm` against the object totals of section 3.2.

### 4.3 USB

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| One KrakenSDR at defaults | 24.0 MB/s |
| USB 2.0 high-speed signalling | 480 Mbit/s (60 MB/s raw) |
| Planning budget per high-speed bus (`daq_preflight.py --usb-budget`) | 35 MB/s, so one unit uses 69 % |
| Two units on one high-speed bus | 48 MB/s, over budget |

List the receivers and their bus with `python3 _daq_core/hw_discover.py --sdr` (JSON, no device opened). Bus speeds are in `/sys/bus/usb/devices/usb*/speed`.

The USB ring absorbs short reader stalls. When the reader lags by the full ring, `rtl_daq.out` counts an overrun, logs `USB ring-buffer overrun ... - raise [daq] usb_ring_buffers (now N)` and stamps the running count into header slot 102. Raise `[daq] usb_ring_buffers` (default 8) and `[daq] usb_async_transfers` (default 12), both 2..64. Each step costs `M*2B` = 2.5 MiB at the defaults. A ring that keeps overrunning while `decimate.out` is busy points at FIR cost, not ring depth (section 2.3).

### 4.4 Network

`:5000` egress exists only with `[data_interface] out_data_iface_type = eth` (section 1).

| Port | Stream | Per-client rate at defaults |
|---|---|---|
| `5000 + N*stride` | `iq_server.out` cf32 frames (eth output only) | `M*fs*8/R` = 96 MB/s |
| `7000` | IQ router fan-in (opt-in) | sum over sources of `M*fs*8/R` |
| `5001`, `5002`, `5003`, `1130` (`+ N*stride`) | control, status, events, ZMQ tuner | negligible |

A nominal GbE link is 125 MB/s before TCP/IP overhead. One default `:5000` client uses 77 % of it. Multi-client `iq_server` (`[data_interface] iq_server_max_clients > 1`) multiplies the egress by the client count.

## 5. Calibration and retune costs

Every ZMQ command to `rtl_daq.out` makes it emit `NO_DUMMY_FRAMES = 5` dummy frames. `hw_controller.py` sends `c` frequency, `g` gain, `a` AGC, `n` noise source and `b` bias tee. `delay_sync.py` sends `s` sample-clock tune during synchronisation. Each dummy frame stands for one DAQ block of `B/fs` = 0.109 s. A dummy frame also resets the rebuffer ring, so the next DATA frame needs a full CPI first.

| Event | Dead time at defaults | Formula |
|---|---|---|
| Any tuner command | 0.546 s of dummy frames | `5*B/fs` |
| CPI refill after the dummy frames | up to 0.437 s | `Ncpi*R/fs` |
| Retune (`FREQ`) | about 1 s plus recalibration | dummy frames + refill; the RF change also restarts calibration in `delay_sync.py`, whose length is not modelled here |

Periodic calibration in `cal_track_mode = 2` (shipped):

| Item | Value | Derivation |
|---|---|---|
| Burst interval | 687 tracking frames = 300 s | `cal_frame_interval * T_fp` |
| Burst length | 10 CAL frames, about 1.1 s | `cal_frame_burst_size`; `rebuffer.out` emits one CAL frame per DAQ block because `corr_size < daq_buffer_size` |
| Dummy frames per burst | 2 x 5 = 1.09 s | noise source on, then off |
| Outage per burst | about 2.2 s, plus up to one CPI refill | burst + dummy frames |
| Duty cycle | about 0.7 % to 0.9 % | outage / 300 s |

These are estimates from the code paths. Measured values are `TBD`.

Planning consequences:

* A frequency schedule (`[schedule]`) pays at least 1 s per hop, plus calibration when `require_cal_on_hop = 1`. Set `dwell_frames` or `dwell_time_sec` well above that.
* `heimdall-ctl recal` sends `RECL` when the server advertises it after XACK, which needs `[calibration] en_wire_recal = 1`. Otherwise it warns and sends `INIT`.
* `INIT` re-enters the `hw_controller.py` FSM. It re-sends the gains and switches the noise source off, so it costs the dummy frames of two tuner commands (at least 0.546 s) plus a CPI refill. It does not make a locked `delay_sync.py` leave tracking, so it does not recalibrate a locked chain.

## 6. FIR and FFT CPU costs

### 6.1 FIR decimation (`decimate.out`)

`decimate.out` filters only DATA frames with `decimation_ratio > 1`. CAL frames and every frame at `R = 1` are only converted from u8 to cf32.

| Engine (`[offload] fir_engine`) | Work per channel per frame | MAC rate, all channels |
|---|---|---|
| `kfr` (default on x86_64 and aarch64) | filters at full input rate, then subsamples: `2*taps*Ncpi*R` | `2*taps*M*fs` |
| `generic` (plain C) | evaluates only the kept outputs: `2*taps*Ncpi` | `2*taps*M*fs/R` |
| `neon` (32-bit ARM, Ne10) | not analysed here | `TBD` |

KFR does `R` times more multiply-accumulates than `generic`, but with SIMD. Which one is faster on a given host is a measurement, not a formula. Results are `TBD`.

The symptom of an FIR that is too slow is USB overruns, not dropped frames: `decimate.out` back-pressures `rebuffer.out` and the USB ring (section 2.3). Watch header slot 102 and `rtl_daq.log` after you raise `fir_tap_size` or `decimation_ratio`.

The `fpga` and `gpu` engines are experimental and not a capacity lever. Uncommenting the FPGA block in `_daq_core/Makefile` fails to link because `hat_gpio_ctrl.o` is not added. Uncommenting the USB3 block builds the no-libusb stub because `USELIBUSB` is never defined.

### 6.2 FFT and correlation (`delay_sync.py`)

`delay_sync.py` runs on one pinned core. It copies each frame once in and once out (40 + 40 MiB per frame at the defaults). At 2.29 frames/s that is about 92 MiB/s each way, 183 MiB/s of memory traffic in total. Its FFT and cross-correlation engines use `[offload] fft_workers` and `[offload] xcorr_workers` threads (default 4). With one pinned core those threads share that core. Widen the core mask (section 10, lever 2) before you raise the worker count. CPU cost per frame is `TBD`.

## 7. Limits enforced by `ini_checker.py`

| Condition | Severity | Message |
|---|---|---|
| `num_ch > 31` | error | channel limit |
| `cpi_size > 2^23` | error | `CPI size must be at most 8388608 (2^23): larger frames overrun the decimator_out/delay_sync_iq shared-memory segments.` |
| `corr_size > 2^23` | error | `Calibration correlation size must be at most 8388608 (2^23): larger frames overrun the decimator_out/delay_sync_iq shared-memory segments.` |
| `fir_tap_size <= decimation_ratio` with `decimation_ratio != 1` | error | `FIR tap size must be higher than the decimation ratio. Please consider increasing the tap size` |
| `T_fp > 8 s` | warning | `the frame period is ... above 8 s` |
| `ctl_request_timeout_sec < 2 * T_fp` | warning | `control verbs will time out on a healthy chain` |

With the default `ctl_request_timeout_sec = 10`, keep `T_fp` at or below 5 s, or raise `[daq] ctl_request_timeout_sec` to at least 2 x `T_fp` (maximum 600). Real output for the shipped config with three keys changed, `cpi_size = 4194304` (2^22), `decimation_ratio = 4` and `fir_tap_size = 32` (`T_fp` = 7.0 s):

```
$ python3 ini_checker.py big.ini no_hw
WARNING: [daq] ctl_request_timeout_sec = 10 is below 2 x the frame period (7.0 s): control verbs will time out on a healthy chain
$ echo $?
0
```

Warnings never change the exit code. The same config with `cpi_size = 16777216` (2^24, still with `fir_tap_size = 32`) fails with exit 1:

```
ERROR:root:CPI size must be at most 8388608 (2^23): larger frames overrun the decimator_out/delay_sync_iq shared-memory segments. Currently it is: '16777216'
WARNING: the frame period is 28.0 s (cpi_size x decimation_ratio / sample_rate), above 8 s: control replies, status refreshes and stall detection all wait frames
WARNING: [daq] ctl_request_timeout_sec = 10 is below 2 x the frame period (28.0 s): control verbs will time out on a healthy chain
```

## 8. Pre-flight check

`Firmware/daq_preflight.py` compares the model of one or more instance configs with what the host has. It reports `need / have / verdict` per resource. Run it from `Firmware/`:

```
usage: daq_preflight.py [-h] [--config INI [INI ...]] [--plus-live]
                        [--add-instances N] [--host-json FILE]
                        [--dump-host-json] [--mode {hw,synthetic}]
                        [--usb-budget MBPS] [--strict] [--json]
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--config INI ...` | instance INIs and/or a `federation.ini` (default `./daq_chain_config.ini`) |
| `--plus-live` | also count the live instances of the host registry (only chains started with `[host] instance_registry = 1`) |
| `--add-instances N` | add N planned copies of the last instance INI, with `serial_base = 1000 + 100*N`, `cpu_cores = 4N..4N+3` and ports `+ N*stride` |
| `--host-json FILE` | use host values from FILE (`-` = stdin) instead of probing this host |
| `--dump-host-json` | print this host's probed values in the `--host-json` schema and exit |
| `--mode hw\|synthetic` | mode of the given instances (synthetic: no USB receivers) |
| `--usb-budget MBPS` | usable MB/s of one USB 2.0 high-speed bus (default 35) |
| `--strict` | count warnings as failures (exit 2) |
| `--json` | print the JSON report |

| Exit | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | every check `ok` (or `skip`) |
| 1 | at least one `warn` |
| 2 | at least one `fail` (or a `warn` with `--strict`) |
| 3 | usage or configuration error |

### 8.1 Checks

| Resource key | need vs have | Verdict rule |
|---|---|---|
| `cores` | `4 * hardware instances` vs `nproc` | `fail` when short, or `warn` when every planned instance sets `allow_core_sharing = allow`; `fail` for a configured core `>= nproc` |
| `core_overlap` | cores shared between instances | `fail` if any sharer sets `refuse`, `ok` if all set `allow`, else `warn` |
| `mem_available` | sum of locked + resident + copies of the new instances, + 512 MiB, vs `MemAvailable` | `fail` when short, `warn` above 80 % |
| `shm_free` | sum of resident sizes vs `/dev/shm` free | `fail` when short |
| `shm_size` | sum of object sizes vs `/dev/shm` size | `warn` when short (only resident pages are allocated) |
| `memlock` | largest per-process locked set (section 2.2) vs `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK` | `ok` when unlimited (`-1`), else `warn` when short; root is exempt |
| `usb_bus:<n>` | USB ingress on bus `n` vs budget (MB/s) | `fail` when over budget: two units on one high-speed bus at defaults fail |
| `usb_unplaced` | receivers whose serial is not attached | `warn` |
| `egress:<nic>` | `:5000` egress vs NIC speed (MB/s, eth output only) | `warn` from 70 % of the link, `fail` above 100 % |
| `ports` | collisions between the enabled ports of the configs, live instances and the coordinator/router ports | `fail` on any collision |
| `serials` | receiver serials claimed by more than one instance | `fail` on any collision |
| `frame_period` | `T_fp` vs 8 s | `warn` above 8 s |
| `router_memory` | router bound (section 3.3) vs `MemAvailable` | `skip` without a `federation.ini` carrying router keys; `fail` when short, `warn` above 80 % |
| `limits` | `num_ch <= 31`, `cpi_size` and `corr_size <= 2^23` | `fail` on any violation |
| `board` | hardware instances on a Raspberry Pi 5 | `warn` for more than one |

Each verdict is one of `ok`, `warn`, `fail`, `skip`. `skip` means the probe was not available, for example `/proc` on macOS or a key absent from `--host-json`. When a resource cannot be checked at all, its key appears without the suffix (`usb_bus`, `egress`) with verdict `skip`.

Real output for the shipped config plus one planned instance, against an 8-core host file with one unit on each of buses 1 and 3 (the install root is shown as `/opt/heimdall`):

```
$ python3 daq_preflight.py --config daq_chain_config.ini --add-instances 1 --host-json x86.json
HeIMDALL DAQ pre-flight - host from --host-json: nproc 8, model -
  instance 0   hw        config  cores 0,1,2,3      ports iq 5000 ctl 5001 zmq 1130  /opt/heimdall/Firmware/daq_chain_config.ini
  instance 1   hw        planned cores 4,5,6,7      ports iq 5100 ctl 5101 zmq 1230  
RESOURCE                   NEED           HAVE  VERDICT NOTE
cores                   8 cores        8 cores  ok      cores in use: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
core_overlap            0 cores        0 cores  ok      
mem_available          1.13 GiB       6.84 GiB  ok      locked + resident of the new instances + 512 MiB headroom
shm_free              360.0 MiB       3.63 GiB  ok      resident shared memory of the new instances
shm_size               1.45 GiB       3.73 GiB  ok      object sizes
memlock               100.0 MiB      unlimited  ok      unlimited
usb_bus:1             24.0 MB/s      35.0 MB/s  ok      instances 0
usb_bus:3             24.0 MB/s      35.0 MB/s  ok      instances 1
egress                        -              -  skip    no instance uses eth output
ports              0 collisions   0 collisions  ok      
serials            0 collisions   0 collisions  ok      
frame_period            0.437 s        8.000 s  ok      warn above 8 s
router_memory                 -              -  skip    no federation.ini with router keys
limits             0 violations   0 violations  ok      
board               2 instances              -  skip    board model not probed
note: 1 planned instance(s) copy /opt/heimdall/Firmware/daq_chain_config.ini with the provisioning defaults (serial_base 1000+100*N, cpu_cores 4N..4N+3)
result: ok (exit 0)
```

With both units on bus 1 the USB row fails:

```
usb_bus:1             48.0 MB/s      35.0 MB/s  fail    instances 0,1; more receivers than one bus carries - move a unit to another controller
result: fail (exit 2)
```

### 8.2 `--json` output

The JSON report carries `schema`, `exit`, `host`, `instances` (each with its ports, cores and `model` byte counts), `resources` and `virtual_bytes`. Each resource has `need`, `have`, `unit`, `verdict` and `note`. Real entries for the shipped config with `out_data_iface_type = eth` on the 8-core host file:

```json
{"egress:eth0": {"need": 96.0, "have": 125.0, "unit": "MB/s", "verdict": "warn", "note": "77 % of link (1 client at cf32)"},
 "memlock": {"need": 104861696, "have": -1, "unit": "bytes", "verdict": "ok", "note": "unlimited"},
 "mem_available": {"need": 877664256, "have": 7340032000, "unit": "bytes", "verdict": "ok", "note": "locked + resident of the new instances + 512 MiB headroom"}}
```

`virtual_bytes.decimator_in_consumer_map` reports the consumer-map size for information only.

### 8.3 Planning on another machine

Probe the target host, copy the file, and run the check where the configs live:

```
target$ python3 daq_preflight.py --dump-host-json > pi4.json
laptop$ python3 daq_preflight.py --config inst0.ini inst1.ini --host-json pi4.json
```

`--host-json -` reads standard input. Every key of the input is optional. A missing key makes its checks `skip`. A present key must have the right type: `"model": null` is a usage error (exit 3), so leave the key out instead.

```json
{"schema": 1, "nproc": 8, "model": "Raspberry Pi 4 Model B Rev 1.4",
 "mem_available": 7340032000, "shm_size": 4000000000, "shm_free": 3900000000,
 "memlock": -1,
 "usb_buses": [{"bus": 1, "speed_mbps": 480, "devices": [{"serial": "1000", "devnum": 3}]}],
 "nics": [{"name": "eth0", "speed_mbps": 1000}],
 "live": []}
```

`--add-instances N` asks "does this host fit N more instances like these". `--plus-live` adds the instances already registered on this host.

### 8.4 `heimdall-ctl capacity`

`heimdall-ctl capacity` runs `<firmware>/daq_preflight.py` in the firmware directory and prints its output unchanged. It forwards `--config`, `--add-instances`, `--host-json` and `--json`. It applies `--strict` itself, through the exit mapping below.

```
heimdall-ctl [--firmware-dir DIR] [--json] [--strict] capacity [--config INI [INI ...]] [--add-instances N] [--host-json FILE]
```

The firmware directory is `--firmware-dir`, else `$HEIMDALL_FIRMWARE`, else the directory of the resolved config, else this source tree's `Firmware/`. `--firmware-dir` is a global flag and must come before `capacity`; after it, the parser exits 2 with `unrecognized arguments`.

| Tool exit | `heimdall-ctl` exit | With `--strict` |
|---|---|---|
| 0 (ok) | 0 | 0 |
| 1 (warnings) | 0 | 1 |
| 2 (failures) | 5 | 5 |
| tool not found | 3 | 3 |
| anything else (for example 3, usage) | 1 | 1 |

### 8.5 Start-time hook (opt-in)

`[host] preflight` controls whether the start script runs the check:

| Value | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `off` (default) | not run |
| `warn` | runs `daq_preflight.py --config daq_chain_config.ini --plus-live`, prints the result, start continues |
| `strict` | as `warn`; a `fail` (exit 2) makes the start script exit 4 |

`daq_start_sm.sh` runs the hook. `daq_synthetic_start.sh` runs it only with `--rt`. A missing `daq_preflight.py` prints `WARN: daq_preflight.py not found; preflight skipped` and the start continues.

### 8.6 Manual checks

These commands read the same host values as the tool. Use them to cross-check a verdict, or on a host without the Python environment. Run them from `Firmware/`:

| Step | Command | Compare with |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `nproc` | at least 4 x hardware instances |
| 2 | `grep MemAvailable /proc/meminfo` | RAM need of section 3.2 |
| 3 | `df -h /dev/shm` | `/dev/shm` resident and object totals of section 3.2 |
| 4 | `ulimit -l` | the largest per-process locked set (section 2.2), or `unlimited` |
| 5 | `python3 _daq_core/hw_discover.py --sdr` and `cat /sys/bus/usb/devices/usb*/speed` | one unit per bus, bus at 480 Mbit/s or faster |
| 6 | `cat /sys/class/net/eth0/speed` (eth output only) | `:5000` egress of section 3.2 |
| 7 | `python3 ini_checker.py daq_chain_config.ini no_hw` | exit 0 |

## 9. Measuring a running chain

### 9.1 What to watch

| Signal | Where | Enable |
|---|---|---|
| USB overruns | header slot 102 (`IQH_RSV_BUFFER_OVERRUN_CNT`), cumulative; `rtl_daq.log` warning lines | always on |
| Decimator output drops | header slot 109 (`IQH_RSV_DECIMATOR_DROP_CNT`), cumulative | `[monitoring] stamp_decimator_drops = 1` |
| `delay_sync.py` output drops, latency, frame rate | `:5002` `METRICS`: `frame_processing_latency_ms`, `frame_throughput_fps`, `dropped_frames_iq`, `dropped_frames_hwc` | `[monitoring] en_monitoring = 1`, `en_metrics = 1`, `en_status_server = 1` |
| Health over a window | `:5002` `STATUS`: `recent_drops`, `drop_window_sec` | as above; `[monitoring] drop_window_sec` (default 60.0) |
| CPI gaps, overruns, decimator drops | `:5002` `STATUS` `counters.cpi_gaps`, `counters.daq_block_gaps`, `counters.buffer_overrun_cnt`, `counters.overrun_invalidated_frames`, `counters.decimator_drops` | as above, plus `[monitoring] status_extended = 1` (and `stamp_decimator_drops = 1` for `decimator_drops`) |
| Frame loss at a consumer | `cpi_index` gaps in the header | always on |

No tool in this release reads header slots from a running stream. Read slot 102 and the `cpi_index` gaps through the extended `STATUS` counters:

```
echo STATUS | nc 127.0.0.1 5002
```

Use `cpi_index` to detect lost frames. Do not use `daq_block_index`: each output frame carries the index of the last DAQ block in its CPI, so it advances by `cpi_size*decimation_ratio/daq_buffer_size` per DATA frame (4 at the defaults).

The shared-memory drop warning (`Dropping frame.. Total: [N]`) is compiled out (`INGORE_FRAME_DROP_WARNINGS 1` in `sh_mem_util.h`). `decimator.log` therefore shows no drops. Use slot 109, `counters.decimator_drops` or the `METRICS` counters instead.

Each `METRICS` entry is `{min, max, avg, p95, count, last}` over the last `metrics_window_size` frames (default 1000):

```
$ echo METRICS | nc 127.0.0.1 5002
{"frame_processing_latency_ms": {"min": ..., "max": ..., "avg": ..., "p95": ..., "count": ..., "last": ...}, ...}
```

`heimdall-ctl metrics` shows the same data as a table (Metric, Min, Avg, P95, Max, Count). `heimdall-ctl --json metrics` prints the raw reply. Values are `TBD` until measured.

Keep `frame_processing_latency_ms` p95 below half of `T_fp`. That is the pass criterion of the planned throughput lane.

### 9.2 IQ client probe

**Planned (WP-20), not yet in this release.** `Firmware/_testing/iq_latency_probe.py` does not exist yet. This section describes the design.

The probe connects like a real `:5000` client (`streaming` handshake, per-frame `IQDownload`). It reports frames, throughput in MB/s, `latency_ms` (receive wall time minus header `time_stamp`, also minus the frame period), `cpi_index` gaps and the slot-102 overrun delta.

```
python3 _testing/iq_latency_probe.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5000 --duration 60 --json
python3 _testing/iq_latency_probe.py --instance 1 --port-stride 100 --duration 60
```

Latency across hosts needs synchronised clocks; see [networking_and_time_sync.md](networking_and_time_sync.html).

### 9.3 Throughput lane

**Planned (WP-17b), not yet in this release.** `test_throughput_lane.py` does not exist yet, and `sudo ./unit_test.sh --sudo` does not write `throughput.json`. This section describes the design.

`test_throughput_lane.py` is a sudo pipeline suite. It runs 300 paced synthetic frames through the real chain. It checks `cpi_index` continuity, zero overruns, bounded drops and `frame_processing_latency_ms` p95 below `0.5 * T_fp`. It writes `Firmware/_testing/test_logs/throughput.json`:

```json
{"date": "...", "host": "...", "nproc": 0, "model": "...", "frames": 300,
 "p50_ms": 0.0, "p95_ms": 0.0, "drops": 0, "overruns": 0, "fps": 0.0}
```

It is planned to run on the target host (Linux, root, built C binaries) with:

```
cd Firmware
sudo ./unit_test.sh --sudo
```

The CI `pipeline` job uploads `Firmware/_testing/test_logs/` as the `pipeline-test-logs` artifact.

### 9.4 Measured results

Each row must cite a `throughput.json` with its date and host. None exists yet.

| Host | Config | fps | p50 ms | p95 ms | drops | overruns | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raspberry Pi 4 | defaults, 1 instance | TBD | TBD | TBD | TBD | TBD | TBD |
| Raspberry Pi 5 | defaults, 1 instance | TBD | TBD | TBD | TBD | TBD | TBD |
| 8-core x86 | defaults, 2 instances | TBD | TBD | TBD | TBD | TBD | TBD |
| CI runner (`pipeline`) | synthetic, 1 instance | TBD | TBD | TBD | TBD | TBD | TBD |

`util/performance_monitor.py` and `Firmware/benchmark_workload.sh` also exist. Their rework to measure through a real `:5000` client is planned. Do not use their current output for sizing.

## 10. Safe throughput levers

Every lever is opt-in. With the key absent, the chain behaves exactly as before.

| # | Lever | Key (default) | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | FFT / correlation workers | `[offload] fft_workers = 4`, `[offload] xcorr_workers = 4` (1..64 or `auto`) | worker threads of `delay_sync.py`'s FFT and correlation engines. `auto` = the count of `[host] delay_sync_cores` when set, else the process affinity size. Results are bit-identical for every value. |
| 2 | `delay_sync.py` core mask | `[host] delay_sync_cores` (empty) | wider `taskset` list for `delay_sync.py` only, so more than one worker runs in parallel |
| 3 | Mode-1 tracking decimation | `[calibration] track_decimation = 1` | in `cal_track_mode = 1`, the IQ tracking check runs every k-th DATA frame; other frames reuse the last flags |
| 4 | Skip the copy on a dropped output buffer | `[offload] skip_copy_on_drop = 0` | when `delay_sync_iq` drops a frame and `en_iq_cal = 0`, process the input in place instead of copying it |
| 5 | USB ring and transfer depth | `[daq] usb_ring_buffers = 8`, `[daq] usb_async_transfers = 12` (2..64) | deeper ring against reader stalls (section 4.3) |
| 6 | Config-sized segments | `[pre_processing] size_segments_from_config = 0` | `1` cuts `decimator_out` from 640 to 80 MiB at defaults; `iq_server.out` then maps exactly the `delay_sync_iq` size |
| 7 | Multi-client `iq_server` | `[data_interface] iq_server_max_clients = 1` (1..64), `iq_server_frame_deadline_ms = 0` (0 = auto: 0.8 x `T_fp`, at least 100 ms) | more than one `:5000` client per instance; a client that has not acknowledged a frame by the deadline is closed. Egress grows per client. |
| 8 | Rebuffer drop path | none (fix) | in drop mode (`rebuffer.out 1`, not used by the start scripts) an undelivered CPI is discarded instead of re-sent |

The largest lever is outside this table: `decimation_ratio`. It cuts egress and `delay_sync.py` work per second by `R` and costs FIR CPU (section 6.1). Set `[pre_processing] fir_tap_size` above the ratio first (for example 64), then re-run `ini_checker.py`. It also cuts the output sample rate and the bandwidth the downstream DSP sees by `R`.

`[pre_processing] fft_workers` and `[calibration] xcorr_workers` are not read by any process. `ini_checker.py` warns: `[pre_processing] fft_workers is not read by any process; use [offload] fft_workers`.

## 11. Core layout and priority knobs

The knobs are in the optional `[host]` section of each instance's `daq_chain_config.ini`. The whole section is opt-in: with it absent, the start scripts behave as before.

| Key | Default | Validation | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cpu_cores` | empty | exactly 4 distinct non-negative ints; each below `nproc` (the `nproc` bound is checked only without `no_hw`) | cores for the tiers rtl_daq, rebuffer+decimate, delay_sync+iq_server, hw_controller. Empty = `(N*4+k) % nproc`. |
| `delay_sync_cores` | empty | comma list of ints | lever 2 above |
| `rt_priority_offset` | 0 | 0..81 | subtracted from every priority (99/94/92/90/88/82) |
| `allow_core_sharing` | `warn` | `warn` \| `refuse` \| `allow` | what to do when instances share cores. At start, `refuse` and `warn` act only with `instance_registry = 1` (section 4.1). `daq_preflight.py` reads it without the registry. |
| `instance_registry` | 0 | 0/1 | write the host registry entry, take the instance lock and the startup mutex; needed for the start-time core-overlap guard and for `--plus-live` |
| `instance_guard` | `legacy` | `legacy` \| `refuse` (`refuse` needs `instance_registry = 1`) | `refuse` refuses a duplicate start of the same instance |
| `preflight` | `off` | `off` \| `warn` \| `strict` | section 8.5 |
| `host_tuning` | `always` | `always` \| `auto` \| `1` \| `0` | `always`: the built-in sysctl, IRQ, usbfs and drop_caches commands. `1`: run `util/host_tuning.sh --apply`. `auto`: as `1` unless host tuning already ran. `0`: skip |
| `usb_irq_core` | empty | int >= 0 | passed to `irq_tuning.sh --usb-core` |
| `usb_controller` | empty | single-line string | passed to `irq_tuning.sh --controller` |
| `health_thread_sched_other` | 0 | 0/1 | `delay_sync.py`'s federation health and registrar threads run as `SCHED_OTHER` instead of inheriting its real-time priority |

`ini_checker.py` validates these keys. See [configuration.md](configuration.html) for the full key reference.

`[host] cpu_cores` exists to move an instance off the default layout, for example off the core that serves the USB interrupts. This 8-core x86 example pins the USB IRQs to core 4 with `usb_irq_core` (passed to `util/irq_tuning.sh` when `host_tuning` runs it) and keeps the busiest tiers of instance 1 off that core. Instance 0 INI (`<root>/Firmware/daq_chain_config.ini`):

```ini
[host]
cpu_cores = 0,1,2,3
```

Instance 1 INI (`<root>/instances/1/Firmware/daq_chain_config.ini`):

```ini
[host]
cpu_cores = 5,6,7,4
usb_irq_core = 4
```

The tier order is rtl_daq, rebuffer+decimate, delay_sync+iq_server, hw_controller. Here instance 1 puts the low-priority `hw_controller.py` (82) on core 4 with the USB IRQs. Its `rtl_daq.out` (99) gets core 5 to itself.

### 11.1 Performance profiles

`config_files/performance/` holds two kinds of files:

| File | Status |
|---|---|
| `minimal.ini`, `balanced.ini`, `maximum.ini` | active `[host]` + `[offload]` snippets. `util/provision_instance.py --profile minimal\|balanced\|maximum` merges them into an instance INI. |
| `minimal.conf`, `balanced.conf`, `maximum.conf` | legacy reference only. No code reads their `[performance]` section. |

| Key | `minimal` | `balanced` | `maximum` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[host] rt_priority_offset` | 4 (tiers 95/90/88/86/84/78) | 0 | 0 |
| `[host] allow_core_sharing` | `warn` | `refuse` | `refuse` |
| `[host] preflight` | `warn` | `warn` | `strict` |
| `[offload] fft_workers`, `xcorr_workers` | 1 | `auto` | `auto` |

`maximum` sets `preflight = strict`: a failed pre-flight blocks the start with exit 4. Pair `maximum` with `--delay-sync-cores` so the `auto` workers get cores of their own. Profile keys are merged after the provisioning defaults and before the explicit flags:

```
sudo python3 util/provision_instance.py --instance 1 --profile balanced            # dry run
sudo python3 util/provision_instance.py --instance 1 --profile balanced --write
```

## 12. Rejected levers

These were evaluated and not built. Each one either changes output bytes or couples a slow consumer back onto USB ingress.

| Lever | Why rejected |
|---|---|
| Zero-copy `delay_sync.py` (hard-linked buffers) | A slow `:5000` client would back-pressure `decimate.out`, `rebuffer.out` and the USB ring under the default drop topology. It also collides with `SharedMemory(create=True)` and the stale-segment unlink in `shmemIface.py`. |
| IQ correction in the decimator | Results match the numba `fastmath` kernel only to 2 ULP, not bit for bit. |
| Header-only passthrough mode | Same flow-control coupling as zero-copy. |
| Polyphase KFR FIR | Not bit-identical to today's output. |
| ci16 egress | Changes the consumer wire format. Left for a future opt-in. |
